differences.title: 1. DATA MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Chronicle stores data as an immutable, append-only log. Each write is a new entry, creating a verifiable history and enabling efficient time-travel queries.
differences.rightDesc: Redis uses a flexible key-value model, supporting various data structures like strings, hashes, lists, sets, and sorted sets for diverse caching and state management needs.

differences.title: 2. PERSISTENCE
differences.leftDesc: Chronicle leverages durable write-ahead logging (WAL) and immutable storage for strong ACID compliance and recovery, ensuring data integrity even during crashes.
differences.rightDesc: Redis offers RDB snapshots and Append Only File (AOF) for persistence, balancing performance with durability, though AOF can be less granular than a true WAL.

differences.title: 3. DATA INTEGRITY
differences.leftDesc: Chronicle uses cryptographic hashing to create tamper-evident logs, providing built-in data integrity and auditability without external mechanisms.
differences.rightDesc: Redis prioritizes speed and is primarily an in-memory cache. Integrity relies on configured persistence mechanisms and client-side validation.

differences.title: 4. QUERYING
differences.leftDesc: Chronicle excels at querying historical states and specific event sequences due to its append-only nature, enabling powerful audit and time-based analysis.
differences.rightDesc: Redis offers fast lookups by key and supports powerful commands for manipulating its data structures, optimized for retrieval speed.

differences.title: 5. USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: Ideal for regulatory compliance, verifiable transaction logs, distributed system state tracking, and applications requiring absolute data immutability and auditability.
differences.rightDesc: Perfect for session management, real-time leaderboards, rate limiting, message queues, and high-performance caching layers to accelerate application responses.

differences.title: 6. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Chronicle scales by distributing the append-only log across nodes, ensuring consistency and providing ordered event streams for distributed applications.
differences.rightDesc: Redis scales via client-side sharding, Redis Cluster, or Sentinel for high availability, distributing data and read operations across multiple instances.

differences.title: 7. MEMORY USAGE
differences.leftDesc: Chronicle is primarily disk-based, allowing for massive datasets that exceed available RAM, with efficient memory mapping for hot data access.
differences.rightDesc: Redis resides primarily in RAM for maximum speed. While it supports persistence to disk, its performance is tied to available memory capacity.
